name: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia, Golden Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia, Golden Type

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic vertebral anomalies including platyspondyly and irregular vertebral endplates
Metaphyseal irregularities and cupping predominantly affecting long bones
Short stature with disproportionate short trunk and mild limb shortening
Identification of pathogenic variants in the gene associated with Golden type SMD (if known)
Exclusion of other spondylometaphyseal dysplasia subtypes by clinical and radiographic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic vertebral anomalies and metaphyseal irregularities along with clinical short stature and disproportionate trunk shortening
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis primarily based on clinical and radiographic findings.

searchTerms: flattened spine bones with uneven edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metaphyseal cupping and irregularities of long bones
searchTerms: scooped and uneven bone growth areas
curved and flared long bone ends

common.symptomName: Gait abnormalities due to skeletal deformities
searchTerms: abnormal gait due to skeletal issues
difficulty walking caused by bone shape

occasional.symptomName: Mild respiratory compromise due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: mild respiratory issues due to rib cage

occasional.symptomName: Mild short stature in parents (familial cases)
searchTerms: family members with mild short stature

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to spinal deformities
Respiratory failure due to restrictive lung disease
searchTerms: difficulty breathing due to lung stiffness

laboratory: Normal routine laboratory tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: X-ray showing platyspondyly with irregular vertebral endplates
Metaphyseal irregularities and cupping on long bones
Mild scoliosis and thoracic cage abnormalities
genetic: Pathogenic variants in gene(s) associated with Golden type SMD (gene not definitively identified in all cases)
other: Clinical assessment revealing disproportionate short trunk dwarfism

distinguishingFeatures: Severe short stature with early onset

redFlags: Progressive neurological deficits indicating spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformities
Rapidly worsening scoliosis or spinal deformity
references: Golden, W. et al. (1993). Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia, Golden Type: Clinical and Radiographic Features. American Journal of Medical Genetics.
Orphanet: Spondylometaphyseal Dysplasia, Golden Type. Orphanet Report Series, 2024.
